deploy-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: P1 - metering/billing anomaly detected for Redwood-hosted metering-pipeline. Automatic alert triggered at 2026-11-03T14:30Z.
Aisha Patel: seeing a flood of overage flags in the dashboard. Token-usage timeline looks spiky starting ~14:05 UTC.
Jesse Lopez: oncall here, taking. any evidence of deploys around 14:00?
Aisha Patel: no prod deploys in the window, last was 09:12 UTC.
billing-bot: snapshot: total_tokens_hour_2026-11-03T14:00 = 12,342,890 (expected ~3.2M) ; overage_flags_emitted = 48 ; reconciliation_job_status = queued
Samir Chen: copying a quick query from the metering-store, looks like duplicate ingestion of the same token batches across two partitions. possible re-ingest.
Samir Chen: SQL snippet: ```SELECT event_id, count(*) as cnt, min(received_at), max(received_at) FROM metering.events WHERE received_at > '2026-11-03T13:50:00Z' GROUP BY event_id HAVING cnt > 1 ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 10;```
Aisha Patel: I see the same event_ids repeating with slightly different partition keys. could be upstream fanout change.
Jesse Lopez: good. quick mitigation idea: pause the reconciler that applies retroactive usage to billing and stop the aggregator job that emits hourly rollups. will that avoid more overage flags?
Samir Chen: yes pause `reconciler-v2` and `hourly-rollup` temporarily. I'll also block downstream flag emission through the safety switch.
Maya R.: tagging support & growth with a short note: affected customers likely to see overage alerts; we should hold billing enforcement while we investigate.
Aisha Patel: working on customer-impact list. preliminary: 4 enterprise accounts (acme-co, helixhealth, corepay, edulog). sending to support slack channel.
Jesse Lopez: executing mitigation commands now: ```# k8s
kubectl -n metering patch deployment reconciler-v2 -p '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'
kubectl -n metering patch deployment hourly-rollup -p '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'```
Samir Chen: done. blocked the emission path: `feature-switch:billing-emission=false` in control plane.
deploy-bot: changelog: reconciler-v2 scaled to 0 (user=jlopez), hourly-rollup scaled to 0 (user=jlopez)
billing-bot: emitted_flags_queue: paused ; queued_flags=102 ; flags_emitted_since_pause=0
Aisha Patel: support has opened private threads w/ the four flagged customers; suggested message: "We detected anomalous usage reporting and have paused enforcement while we investigate." Should we include ETA?
Jesse Lopez: put ETA = 2 hours for initial root-cause and next update.
Samir Chen: quick root-cause hypothesis: a misconfiguration in the ingress event de-duplication TTL + a hot reingest job replayed a day's worth of events into two partitions. dedupe service was upgraded yesterday to v1.4.3 with a TTL default change. the replay code uses event fingerprinting that depends on TTL window. result: same physical events counted twice.
Aisha Patel: any proof of the replay? logs?
Samir Chen: paste logs: ```[2026-11-03T14:03:21Z] replay-job-98 INFO replayer: ingesting batch=98 event_count=24832 src=archive-partition-20261102
[2026-11-03T14:03:21Z] dedupe-1 WARN miss: key=sha256:abc123 ttl_ms=0 -> allow
[2026-11-03T14:03:22Z] ingestion INFO wrote_to_partition p=8 offset=129384
[2026-11-03T14:05:12Z] ingestion INFO wrote_to_partition p=2 offset=56412
```
Jesse Lopez: ok that lines up. plan: 1) keep reconciler paused, 2) run a de-dup dry-run to compute delta (no writes), 3) start backfill-correct only for undercounted periods, 4) hold billing enforcement & notify customers.
Maya R.: I pushed a draft notice to status.redwood.ai and sent to support to use as a template.
Aisha Patel: I'm running the dry-run: `python tools/metering/dedupe_dryrun.py --start 2026-11-03T13:50Z --end 2026-11-03T14:20Z --limit 100000`
Samir Chen: output shows approx +9.4M duplicate tokens in that window. that's consistent with the spike.
Jesse Lopez: message to legal/finance: don't invoice any overage flags generated after 14:03 UTC until we complete reconciliation. tagging @finance-dot.
deploy-bot: incident-created: INC-2026-11-03-2389 (owner=jlopez)
Aisha Patel: created internal incident page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INCIDENTS-2389 (short summary attached).
Samir Chen: initial RCA notes: root cause = replay + dedupe TTL change; contributing = no canary on replayer job that validates dedupe idempotency; gap = no immediate safety circuit to stop replays when dedupe mismatch rate > 1%.
Jesse Lopez: remediation actions (short-term): 1) reconfigure dedupe TTL to previous safe value 2) add pre-replay canary that runs a small sample 3) implement queued flag threshold that auto-pauses emission.
Aisha Patel: longer-term: add telemetry alert for unusual token deltas (>3x baseline) and add better staging tests for replay path. Also propose a post-incident billing reconciliation playbook so support has templates for customer outreach and crediting.
Maya R.: support will offer pro-rated credits for affected customers and update their tickets with ETA 2 hours.
Samir Chen: will own the patch to dedupe service (assigning to samir). ETA for patch + canary = EOD.
Jesse Lopez: closing loop: I'm keeping the incident open until reconciler backfill completes and we verify corrected totals. next update in 30m. tagged incident channel with :hourglass_flowing_sand:.
Aisha Patel: thanks team. logging this thread into the incident doc.
billing-bot: post-mitigation snapshot after pause: total_tokens_hour_2026-11-03T14:00 = 12,342,890 ; projected_corrected_total = 2,942,123 ; duplicates_detected = 9,400,767
Jesse Lopez: final quick note to ops: ensure billing enforcement flag remains off until `reconcile/confirm` step done. I'll transition to oncall follow-up shift at 15:00 UTC. @Samir Chen you'll pick up the RCA work.
Samir Chen: acknowledged. starting the dedupe patch branch now.
Maya R.: posting status update to customers and internal comms.
Aisha Patel: last_msg: incident status = mitigation in place; customer impact = transient false overage alerts for 4 ent accounts (no charges applied); owner = Jesse Lopez; next update 15:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:"
